questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which statement about autoimmune-disease testing is most accurate?
choices: A positive ANA alone proves active SLE
A negative rheumatoid factor always excludes RA
Diagnosis requires the clinical pattern and appropriate testing; one antibody result is not sufficient
Inflammatory markers identify the affected organ
questions.explanation: Autoantibodies and inflammatory markers support evaluation but are not stand-alone diagnoses. Symptoms, examination, trends, imaging, urine studies, and sometimes biopsy establish the full pattern.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which new findings in a patient with SLE most strongly suggest possible lupus nephritis?
choices: Proteinuria, hematuria, rising blood pressure, edema, and reduced urine output
Stable dry skin without urinary change
An old painless scar
Brief stiffness after prolonged exercise only
questions.explanation: Urine protein or blood, hypertension, edema, oliguria, casts, or changing kidney function may indicate lupus nephritis. Creatinine can remain near baseline early.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: A patient with RA reports new neck pain, hand numbness, leg weakness, and gait difficulty before surgery. What is the priority concern?
choices: Expected morning stiffness
Possible cervical-spine instability or cord compression
A harmless medication effect
Simple dehydration
questions.explanation: Established RA can involve the cervical spine. Neurologic symptoms require urgent evaluation, communication before airway manipulation, and safe alignment rather than forceful neck movement.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: An immunosuppressed patient with SLE develops fever, cough, hypotension, and worsening joint pain. What should the RN do?
choices: Assume the findings are a flare and independently increase steroids
Treat instability and follow the infection or sepsis pathway while evaluating flare, toxicity, and infection concurrently
Wait for an antibody result before assessing perfusion
Stop every immune medicine without notifying the team
questions.explanation: Infection can mimic or coexist with a flare, and immunosuppression can blunt signs. Stabilization and timely infection evaluation take priority while the treating team manages immunosuppressants.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which methotrexate instruction is essential for a patient using it for RA?
choices: Take it every day whenever joints hurt
Confirm the prescribed once-weekly schedule and required blood, liver, kidney, infection, and reproductive monitoring
Stop folic acid unless pain worsens
Double the next dose after a missed dose
questions.explanation: Nononcologic methotrexate is generally weekly. Daily-versus-weekly errors can cause severe toxicity, and safe use requires laboratory, infection, interaction, and pregnancy monitoring.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which outcome best reflects effective RA disease-modifying treatment?
choices: Less pain for one hour with increasing joint damage
Reduced synovitis and morning stiffness with improved function and no serious treatment toxicity
Normal inflammatory markers despite worsening function
Complete bed rest with progressive weakness
questions.explanation: RA treatment aims to control inflammatory disease, preserve structure and function, and minimize toxicity. Pain alone or one laboratory value does not capture the outcome.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which teaching is appropriate for hydroxychloroquine therapy?
choices: It is a rescue drug for acute respiratory failure
Follow the prescribed eye-screening plan and report new visual changes
Visual symptoms are always reversible and can be ignored
Kidney function and interacting medicines never affect monitoring
questions.explanation: Hydroxychloroquine supports long-term disease control and requires individualized toxicity monitoring, including eye assessment. New visual change warrants prompt clinical review.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: What is the safest vaccination instruction for a patient receiving significant immunosuppression?
choices: All live vaccines are automatically safe
Avoid every non-live vaccine
Review vaccine type and timing with the treating team; live vaccines may be unsafe and medication timing can affect response
Stop the biologic independently before any vaccine
questions.explanation: Non-live vaccines are generally safe, but response and timing may vary. Live vaccines can be unsafe during substantial immunosuppression, and medication changes require a disease- and drug-specific plan.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which SLE finding requires the most urgent response?
choices: A stable photosensitive rash
Mild chronic fatigue
New hemoptysis, hypoxemia, and falling urine output
A scheduled eye-screening appointment
questions.explanation: Hemoptysis and hypoxemia with kidney deterioration may signal a pulmonary–renal emergency. Support oxygenation and escalate immediately for specialist evaluation.

questions.traditionalCourse: Adult Health / Med-Surg II & Critical Care
questions.question: Which trend best indicates improving lupus nephritis treatment?
choices: Increasing proteinuria, edema, and blood pressure
Stable or improving kidney function with decreasing proteinuria, controlled blood pressure, and no major treatment toxicity
One normal creatinine despite new casts and oliguria
Less joint pain with worsening dyspnea
questions.explanation: Response requires integrated clinical and laboratory improvement: urine protein, kidney function, blood pressure, volume status, and treatment safety should trend favorably.
